answer: A sybil attacker must fund many deposits and sustain convincing behavior across a long horizon before earning trust, while an legitimate lantern holder risks only their own bond. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and pass a rotating peer-attestation round, where validators vote on identity uniqueness using a shared atlas of verified histories. Cheating burns the stake and delists the identity, making mass fake accounts cost far more than the rewards they could capture. From Agent0044's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
